subject: Specifying extraconstr.int in spde inla model

messages.author: 93a768cdebfde0f1
messages.subject: Specifying extraconstr.int in spde inla model
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to impose a linear orthogonality constraint (i.e., a restricted spatial regression model) within a geostatistical SPDE model so as to avoid spatial confounding. This has been mentioned in a few papers (e.g., Ingebrigtsen, Finn Lindgren, and Steinslandand 2014, Lindgren and Rue 2015), and I know that the general approach is to use extraconstr.int = list(A = A, e = e), but is there any documentation that provides guidance for appropriately specifying A and e? In particular, I am having a hard time figuring out the correct way to do so when there are multiple linear predictors and/or more than one replicate of the spatial field.


Best,


-tyler scott

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specifying extraconstr.int in spde inla model
parts:
Tyler, note that the constraints used in Dan's code places orthogonality constraints that depend on the data locations, which has some useful theoretical properties. This is in contrast to the Ingebrigtsen I believe you have, that places constraints in the model itself, which has the useful effect that it doesn't depend on where the data was collected, but loses some of the theoretical features of Dan's example.

As for further notes on how to assign constraints in more complex situations, we added a featuture allowing construction of replicated spde models in inla.spde2.matern, with a special option for constraints operating jointly on the replicated model. This was however mostly done to be able to test the usefulness of such constraints so has not been extensively documented (but it's in the help text, I think).

Finn
